# Sort

## Summary
The shared sort verb: one type-aware comparator so every list orders the same way. `sortBy(items, accessor, direction)` sorts stably; `compareValues` compares numbers numerically, Dates by time, strings with numeric-aware locale rules ("2" before "10"), booleans false-first. The two rules apps kept getting wrong are pinned: null/undefined/empty sort LAST in either direction (an unfilled field never floats to the top because the column flipped), and ties keep incoming order so a secondary sort survives. Holes in the item list (unloaded links) are skipped, not crashed on.

## Usage
```ts
import sortBy from '@cardstack/catalog/utils/sort';
import { priorityRank, PriorityField } from '@cardstack/catalog/fields/priority/priority';

let byDue = sortBy(tasks, (t) => t.dueDate, 'asc');      // undated tasks last
let byPriority = sortBy(byDue, (t) => priorityRank(PriorityField, t.priority));
```
Four shipped apps re-derived per-column sorting before this existed (the second-highest demand count on the P1 list); the Table block's `sortValue` columns are the natural feed.

## Non-goals
Not a query: server-side ordering belongs to the search index's `sort` expressions, whose catalog surface is `components/sort.gts` (`sortByCardTitleAsc`, `SortMenu`) — that builds an index `Sort` expression and its picker UI, this orders an array already in hand, and the two paths are one character apart — this is for lists already in hand. No natural-language collation options beyond locale defaults; a consumer with a bespoke collation passes a pre-computed sort key through the accessor instead.

**On `specType`.** This is a plain module, not an invokable `Command`. The base `SpecType` enum is card / field / component / app / command and has no slot for a helper module, so `command` is the least wrong value — but anything enumerating command Specs to find something callable will surface this one, and it is not.
